Authorizes the Defense Department to support the counterdrug and counter transnational organized crime work of other federal agencies and of state, local, and foreign law enforcement, when they ask for it.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 104 Stat. 1485](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/104/1485){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 10 U.S.C. 284; 10 U.S.C. 124](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/10/284?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Support includes transport, equipment maintenance, training, intelligence analysis, and aerial and ground reconnaissance.
- Sec. 284(b)(7): construction of roads, fences, and lighting to block drug smuggling corridors across U.S. borders.
- Support to foreign agencies requires consultation with the Secretary of State.
- 10 U.S.C. 124 separately makes the department the lead federal agency for detecting and monitoring drug traffic by air and sea.

## Why it matters

It is a support authority: it works within the limits of the [Posse Comitatus Act](posse-comitatus-1878.qmd) and does not authorize the use of force. In 2019 it was used, together with [Section 2808](sec2808-milcon-1982.qmd), to redirect defense funds to border barriers. Overseas, it overlaps with [Chapter 16 of Title 10](seccoop-2016.qmd).

## Current status

In force. It began as Section 1004 of the FY1991 defense authorization and was made permanent in Title 10 by the FY2017 act.
